extracted.intended_audience: general politically-interested British readers and reformers (Victorian-era public)
extracted.subtask_description: A polemical essay diagnosing the failures of British government offices (Downing Street, Colonial, Foreign, Home) and prescribing priorities and principles for administrative reform and more effective governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law must aim at the supreme offender
rubrics_metrics.description: Laws should target the 'supreme scoundrel' (major systemic wrongdoers) rather than only the petty or lowest scoundrel who robs shop-tills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid making law that only punishes minor criminals while allowing powerful offenders to prosper in high places; legal reform must aspire to identify and punish the principal sources of injustice rather than merely the visible small offenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human law must align with moral (Heaven's) ends
rubrics_metrics.description: If human law loses sight of moral purpose it becomes diabolic; laws that decree injustice under a legal form are among the worst evils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislation and administration should be guided by a sincere vision of justice and moral ends—requiring reverence, pious earnestness, and wisdom—rather than mere formal procedure or tradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address root causes (work at the well-heads)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reformers should focus on the chief fountains and real sources of social ills, not on peripheral, downstream tinkering with symptoms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stop 'puddling in the embouchures' and attempting to salvage broken waifs; strike at the main institutions and causes that generate widespread misery to achieve meaningful improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritise administrative (executive) reform over parliamentary tinkering
rubrics_metrics.description: A reformed Executive/administration is more crucial than procedural or electoral reforms of Parliament alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improving how the nation is administered (the Acting-Apparatus) will have greater practical effect than improving the talking-and-debating mechanisms of Parliament; resources should be directed to hire and organize competent administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer an Acting-Apparatus to a Talking-Apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: The government should be structured to act effectively rather than merely to debate and produce rhetorical displays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value and design institutions for decisive practical action and management rather than privileging those who excel only at talking, protocol, or ceremonious 'having the honor to be'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select and retain highly capable, practical administrators
rubrics_metrics.description: Downing Street needs 'Herculean men'—practical, courageous administrators acquainted with what effective management requires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appoint men of proven practical ability who will courageously clean out entrenched inefficiencies and overhaul operations, rather than rewarding orators, theatricals, or mere social standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine and do the right kind of work centrally
rubrics_metrics.description: Central offices must focus only on work essential to the national interest; many tasks currently handled centrally should be left to local or colonial authorities or not handled at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinize each function: if a matter (e.g., many colonial questions or minutiae of foreign protocol) should be decided locally or avoided, cease central interference and conserve central energy for truly vital concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure work is competently and promptly done
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative tasks must not be delayed, neglected, or bungled; they require sufficient intellect and ability to be handled properly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid assigning important tasks to incapable hands; create incentives and structures so that competent people do the work and maintain standards of speed and accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rewarding passivity and quiet incompetence
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference for quiet, compliant subordinates (who 'pass' work through) leads to systemic decline; administrations should not prize docility over ability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not favor passive 'safe' employees whose chief virtue is not to trouble superiors; instead recruit and empower skilled, energetic staff even if they challenge inherited routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate pedantry and rule-bound habit (the Pedant darkness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrenched pedantry—clerks and officials hiding behind traditions and habitual procedures—blocks common-sense improvement and produces ineffective, daedalean bureaucracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break the hold of inapplicable traditions and habitudes; encourage practical common-sense, daylight scrutiny, and willingness to discard useless formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combat systemic stupidity and self-conceit
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief administrative enemy is darkness of mind—various forms of stupidity, especially where pedantry believes itself to be wisdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institute selection, accountability, and oversight to reduce self-conceit and intellectual blindness among administrators; prefer clear-seeing minds that face facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughly scrutinize offices to discover real functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reform must begin with faithful inspection of what offices actually do—looking through cobweb veils to detect the true facts beneath traditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reforms based on impression or prestige; use deep, fact-based inquiry to reveal the real tasks, redundancies, and misallocations of central offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clean out red-tape and accumulated bureaucratic waste
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative establishments are clogged with 'dead pedantries' and 'guano mountains' of accumulated nonsense which must be removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purge useless formalities, obsolete procedures, and the accumulated detritus of centuries; return offices to their original, practical functions and clear surfaces for efficient operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central government should focus on vital domestic interests
rubrics_metrics.description: The nation's attention and resources ought to be devoted to pressing domestic crises (e.g., famine, urban destitution) rather than trivial foreign protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid disproportionate focus on remote diplomatic theater or ceremonial interventions when urgent national problems (the 'Irish Giant' of despair) demand action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use cost-effective, honest channels for foreign intelligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Many functions of resident ambassadors can be handled more cheaply and truthfully by well-selected newspaper correspondents or reporters stationed abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider replacing some resident diplomatic apparatus with journalists/correspondents who are cheaper in both money and in the expense of falsity and hypocrisy; send ambassadors only for great occasions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit central ruling body to a small competent core
rubrics_metrics.description: A small group (ten, twelve, or six men) of abler administrators would better manage national affairs than large, ineffectual bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentrate executive responsibility in a compact, capable Acting-Apparatus rather than diffuse it across many actors whose chief talent is debate or ceremony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid governing as 'No-Government' by neglect and ritual
rubrics_metrics.description: A government that only stages parliamentary palaver and leaves practical management to habit risks collapse and social ruin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure governance includes real management capacity and measured action; if the office of government is reduced to ceremony, replace it with functioning institutions or accept the peril.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appoint administrators who tremble before duty, not pedantry
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaders should fear being mere 'inane phantasms' leaving paltry contributions to guano mountains; their priority must be living service to the public good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate devotion to duty, courage to cleanse entrenched corruption, and disdain for self-serving ritual; effective leaders accept hard, unglamorous work to restore functionality.
